mainTopic: Why torches announced only חסר months, the types of cedar used for them, and רבי יוחנן's teachings drawn from the trees in ישעיהו
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of the torches (משואות) lit on mountaintops to announce ראש חודש. Torches were lit only after a חסר month. The גמרא shows why lighting for every month could be misread, and why lighting only for מלא months would cost people two days of work, as אביי explains. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's long poles. רב יהודה counts four types of cedar, while the school of רב counts ten, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו plus three added trees. One of the added trees is coral, which leads to a side discussion about how coral is pulled from the sea and how valuable it is. רבי יוחנן then gives three teachings: the trees taken from ירושלים will be returned, the myrtle in the wilderness as a picture of learning and teaching תורה, and nothing can replace רבי עקיבא and his colleagues. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks what בית בלתין is. רב's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Lighting after a full month would confuse people when שבת gets in the way
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the answer begun on the previous amud. If torches were lit for a מלא month and the lighting had to be pushed off because of שבת, people would not know how to read the signal.
steps.simpleTranslation: People would come to make a mistake. They would say: maybe this month is חסר, and they didn't light yesterday only because it was impossible on שבת. Or maybe the month is מלא, and they are lighting at the right time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the torches can't be used to signal a מלא month. A late lighting after שבת could be read two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting after שבת looks the same whether the month was חסר and the lighting was delayed, or the month was מלא and the lighting came on time. A signal that can mean two things is useless. So חכמים set the torches only for a חסר month, and no torches means the month was מלא.

keyTerms.meaning: to make a mistake, to get confused

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: a חסר month has 29 days and a מלא month has 30. The torches tell people about the month that just ended.

phrases.english: to make a mistake, for they will say:
This month is deficient (29 days),
and the reason it was not done yesterday
phrases.notes: 'Yesterday' is שבת, when lighting torches is not allowed.

phrases.english: is because it was impossible.
Or perhaps it is a full month (30 days),
and they are doing it at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the preceding text on why torches are not lit for a מלא month.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lighting for a מלא month could be pushed off by שבת, and then the signal would have two possible meanings.

steps.title: Proposal: light for every month but skip when שבת gets in the way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests lighting torches for both מלא and חסר months, and skipping completely in the problem case where ראש חודש falls on ערב שבת. People would figure out from the missing torches that the month was חסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them light for both a full month and a deficient month. When ראש חודש falls on ערב שבת, let them not light at all. Since we don't light on מוצאי שבת, and we normally do light for a full month, people will know that the month is deficient!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the current system by offering a different one that seems to avoid the confusion from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in Step 1 was a lighting moved to מוצאי שבת. The proposal is to never light late at all. Then the only month with no torches would be the special שבת case, and people would read the missing signal as 'חסר'.

phrases.english: So let them do it for both a full month and a deficient month,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מִקְּלַע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: and when ראש חודש falls on Shabbat eve,
let them not do it at all.
And since we do not do it on Saturday night,
and we normally do it for a full month,
people will surely know that it is deficient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different system meant to avoid the confusion described in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that torches are lit only for a חסר month.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only trouble is a lighting delayed by שבת, skip that one case entirely. Then lighting for every month would still give a clear signal.

steps.title: People might think the torches were just prevented
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proposal. If no torches appear, people might think the month was מלא and the lighting simply didn't happen because something went wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, people would come to make a mistake. They would say: this month is full, and the reason they didn't light is that they were held back by something beyond their control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proposal from Step 2 and shows it still leaves room for confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the proposal, torches go up every month, so missing torches are supposed to mean 'חסר'. But when people normally see torches every month, a month with none looks like something went wrong, like the lighters being stopped. They might then assume the month was מלא, so the confusion from Step 1 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: to be held back by circumstances beyond one's control (from the word אונס)

phrases.english: Even so, they will come to make a mistake, for they will say:
This month is full,
and the reason they did not do it
is that they were prevented by circumstances beyond their control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal from Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the proposed system still allows confusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Missing torches would clearly tell people the month was חסר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Missing torches could be blamed on an accident, so people might wrongly think the month was מלא.

steps.title: Proposal: light only for full months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests the opposite of the actual rule: light torches only for a מלא month and never for a חסר one.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them light only for a full month, and not light for a deficient month at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another possible system. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem is people misreading signals, why not just flip the system? Light only for מלא months. The גמרא is asking why חכמים chose חסר months as the ones to signal.

phrases.english: So let them do it for a full month,
and not do it for a deficient month at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֶיעְבֵּיד אַמָּלֵא, וְלָא לֶיעְבֵּיד אַחָסֵר כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'both months' idea was rejected, the גמרא tries the opposite of the actual rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to signal חסר months instead of מלא months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flipping the system so only מלא months are signaled seems just as workable. So why prefer חסר?

steps.title: אביי: people would lose two days of work
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that signaling only מלא months would leave people unsure for two days each time, so they would stop working for both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because that would cause the people to stop working for two days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers Step 4 and explains why חכמים chose to light torches for חסר months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People held back from some work on ראש חודש. If only מלא months were signaled, people would have to treat both the 30th and the 31st as possible ראש חודש until they knew which it was, and lose two days of work. When torches go up after a חסר month, people know right away that the 30th was ראש חודש, and they can go back to work the next day.
steps.whatToRemember: Torches are lit only after a חסר month. Lighting for every month could be misread, and lighting only for מלא months would cost people two days of work, as אביי says.
steps.whyThisMatters: The torch system was built both to send a clear signal and to protect people's livelihood, so ראש חודש would not cost them more work days than it had to.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Because of the stopping of work
for the people for two days.
phrases.notes: People held back from some work on ראש חודש. Without a signal on the 30th, they'd hold back on both the 30th and the 31st.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל מְלָאכָה לָעָם שְׁנֵי יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proposal in Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason based on what each system would cost people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signaling only מלא months would work just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Signaling only מלא months would cost people two days of work, while signaling חסר months lets them go back to work sooner.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: four types of cedar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about lighting torches with long poles, and רב יהודה lists four kinds of ארז.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: How did they light the torches? They brought long poles, and so on. רב יהודה said: There are four types of cedar: ארז, קתרום, עץ שמן, and ברוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the one describing how the torches were made. רב יהודה explains which woods count as 'cedar' for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the poles were made of ארז, cedar. רב יהודה teaches that 'cedar' is really a family of four trees, so any of them would work. This opens a short side discussion about tree names.

keyTerms.meaning: Torches or signal fires lit on hilltops
Cedars, used here for a whole family of trees
A tree in the cedar family whose identity the גמרא will discuss

phrases.english: How would they light the torches?
They would bring long poles, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' means the גמרא quotes only the start of the משנה line, which goes on to say the poles were of cedar.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
There are four types of cedar:
Cedar, katrom, pinewood, and cypress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about which months got torches and turns to the משנה's description of how the torches were made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cedar family has four types: ארז, קתרום, עץ שמן, ברוש.

steps.title: Identifying the tree called קתרום
steps.stepSummary: Three opinions give the everyday name of the tree קתרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קתרום? רב said: it is the אדרא tree. The school of רבי שילא says: it is the מבליגא tree. And some say: it is the גולמיש tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unfamiliar word קתרום from רב יהודה's list by giving its everyday Aramaic name. Three different identifications are offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קתרום was not a common word, so the גמרא matches it to trees people knew. This is a simple disagreement about which real tree the name refers to, not about any law.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree name, רב's identification of קתרום
A tree name, the school of רבי שילא's identification

phrases.english: Katrom: Rav said it is the adra tree.
The school of Rabbi Sheila says: the mavliga tree.
And some say: this is the gulmish tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains one of the four trees רב יהודה just listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קתרום is identified as אדרא (רב), מבליגא (school of רבי שילא), or גולמיש (some say).

steps.title: The school of רב counts ten types of cedar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבה בר רב הונא, quoting the school of רב, disagrees: there are ten types of cedar, learned from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבה בר רב הונא. For רבה בר רב הונא said that they say in the school of רב: There are ten types of cedar, as it says: 'I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the cypress, the תדהר, and the תאשור together.' Each tree is then given its Aramaic name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה's count of four is argued with by another teaching that counts ten. That teaching uses a פסוק and then translates each tree into Aramaic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said four types; the school of רב says ten. Their source is a פסוק that lists trees together, which they read as all belonging to the cedar family. The Aramaic names tell us which real trees are meant.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees (this opinion argues with another)
A tree in the פסוק, here identified as שאגא
A tree in the פסוק, here identified as שוריבנא

steps.confusionAlert: In this discussion, 'ארזים' means a whole family of trees, not just the single tree called ארז. That is why myrtle and acacia can be counted as 'types of cedar.'

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabba bar Rav Huna.
phrases.notes: 'This' means רב יהודה's count of four types.

phrases.english: For Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
They say in the school of Rav:
There are ten types of cedar,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֶתֵּן בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶרֶז שִׁטָּה וַהֲדַס וְעֵץ שָׁמֶן
phrases.english: as it says: 'I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the oil tree;'

phrases.aramaic: אָשִׂים בָּעֲרָבָה בְּרוֹשׁ תִּדְהָר וּתְאַשּׁוּר יַחְדָּו״.
phrases.english: 'I will set in the desert the cypress, the tidhar, and the te'ashur together.'
Erez is arza; shitta is turnita;
hadas is asa; etz shemen is afarsema;
berosh is berata; tidhar is shaga;
te'ashur is shurivna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opinion that argues with רב יהודה's count of four.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the school of רב there are ten types of cedar, based on ישעיהו 41:19.

steps.title: But the פסוק lists only seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the trees in the פסוק add up to seven, not ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are only seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts the trees in the פסוק and finds only seven, which doesn't match the claim of ten. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רב said ten types and gave the פסוק as the source. But the פסוק names only seven trees, so the source seems to fall three short.

phrases.english: These are only seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of ten given in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of the school of רב that there are ten types of cedar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק brought as the source lists only seven trees, so it cannot support a count of ten.

steps.title: רב דימי adds three more trees
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that three more trees were added to the seven: אלונים, אלמונים, and אלמוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: They added to them אלונים, אלמונים, and אלמוגין. אלונים are בוטמי, אלמונים are בלוטי, and אלמוגין are כסיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question by naming three more trees that were added to the list of seven. The גמרא then gives each one's Aramaic name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven from the פסוק are only part of the list. רב דימי reports that three more trees were added to them, which brings the total to ten.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
They added to them alonim, almonim, and almugin.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the seven trees from the פסוק, so now the count reaches ten.

phrases.english: Alonim are butmei; almonim are balutei;
almugin are kasita.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: הוֹסִיפוּ עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that the פסוק lists only seven.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completes the list by adding trees not named in that פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of ten seemed to come only from the פסוק, which names seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three more trees were added to the seven, making ten.

steps.title: A second version of the added three
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the three added trees are ארונים, ערמונים, and אלמוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: ארונים, ערמונים, and אלמוגין. ארונים are ערי, ערמונים are דולבי, and אלמוגין are כסיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב דימי's answer with a slightly different set of three added trees. Again each is given its Aramaic name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that three trees were added and that one of them is אלמוגין. They differ only on the other two trees.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה counts four types of cedar. The school of רב counts ten: seven from the פסוק in ישעיהו plus three added ones. The two versions of the added three disagree only about two of them, and both include אלמוגין.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Arunim, armonim, and almugin.
Arunim are arei; armonim are dulvei;
almugin are kasita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of the answer in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same answer of adding three trees, with a different list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק alone gives only seven trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three added trees are ארונים, ערמונים, and אלמוגין.

steps.title: What is צי אדיר?
steps.stepSummary: Since coral came up, the גמרא quotes a פסוק about a 'צי אדיר' and רב explains it as a big ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a mighty ship will not pass through it': רב said, this is a large ship, a בורני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a side comment, explaining the words 'צי אדיר' from a פסוק. רב says it means a large ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is linked to the mention of אלמוגין (coral) just before. רב identifies the 'mighty ship' of the פסוק as a known kind of large vessel called a בורני.

phrases.english: 'And a mighty ship will not pass through it':
Rav said: This is a large burni ship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side point linked to the mention of אלמוגין (coral) just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'צי אדיר' of the פסוק is a large ship called a בורני.

steps.title: How do they bring up the coral?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the coral is actually harvested.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short practical question: how do people get coral up from the bottom of the sea? This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coral was one of the three trees added to the list in Step 10, and Step 12 brought in the big ship. Now the גמרא wants to know how that ship is used to harvest coral.

phrases.english: How do they do it?
phrases.notes: He means: how do they harvest the coral that came up in the last steps?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the mention of the big ship and asks how it is used for coral.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of harvesting coral from the sea floor.

steps.title: Sinking and raising the ship to pull up coral
steps.stepSummary: Thousands of men load a ship with sand until it sinks. A diver ties the coral to the ship, the sand is thrown out, and the rising ship rips the coral loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: They bring six thousand men for twelve months, and some say twelve thousand men for six months. They load the ship with sand until it sinks. A diver goes down, ties flax ropes onto the coral, and ties the ropes to the ship. Then they throw the sand out, and as the ship rises it uproots the coral and brings it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question step by step. The ship is sunk with sand, tied to the coral, and then lightened so it floats up and pulls the coral out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick is to use the ship's own rising force as a lifting machine. The two numbers of workers are really the same total amount of work, six thousand men for a full year or twelve thousand for half a year. The point is to show how hard and costly it is to get coral, which leads into the next step about its value.

phrases.english: They bring six thousand men
for the twelve months of the year,
and some say: twelve thousand men
for six months of the year,
and they load it with sand until it sinks.
Then a diver goes down
and ties flax ropes onto the coral,
and ties them to the ship.
Then they take the sand and throw it overboard,
and as it rises, it uproots the coral and brings it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיְיתוּ שֵׁית אַלְפֵי גַּבְרֵי בִּתְרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ship is sunk with sand, tied to the coral by a diver, and then lightened so it rises and uproots the coral.

steps.title: How valuable coral is, and where it comes from
steps.stepSummary: Coral is worth twice its weight in silver. There are three ports: two Roman ports that bring up coral and one Persian port that brings up pearls, called the royal port.
steps.simpleTranslation: Coral is traded for twice its weight in silver. There are three ports. Two belong to the Romans and one to the Persians. The Roman ones bring up coral, the Persian one brings up pearls, and it is called the royal port.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds more facts about coral: how much it is worth and which ports produce it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After describing the huge effort it takes, the גמרא shows the reward: coral is worth double its weight in silver. It also contrasts the Roman ports, which produce coral, with the Persian port, which produces pearls and has a royal name.

phrases.english: And it is exchanged for twice its weight in silver.
There are three ports:
two belong to the Romans
and one belongs to the Persians.
The Roman ones bring up coral,
the Persian one brings up pearls,
and it is called the royal port.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the value and sources of the coral that was just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coral is worth twice its weight in silver. It comes from two Roman ports, while the Persian royal port produces pearls.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole coral discussion, from Step 12 to here, is a side-trip. It started because coral, אלמוגין, was one of the trees added to the list of cedars.

steps.title: Every acacia tree taken from Jerusalem will be returned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that הקב"ה will return to ירושלים every שיטה tree that the nations took. He learns this from the פסוק of the trees, where מדבר means ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Every single acacia tree that the nations took from ירושלים, הקב"ה will one day return to it. As it says, "I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia." And "wilderness" means ירושלים, as it says, "Zion has become a wilderness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק of the trees from ישעיהו, and רבי יוחנן learns a promise about ירושלים from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says הקב"ה will plant trees, including the שיטה, "in the wilderness." A second פסוק calls ציון a wilderness, so רבי יוחנן reads the first פסוק as speaking about ירושלים. The trees planted there are understood as the ones that were taken away being given back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Every single acacia tree
that the nations took from Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לָהּ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will one day return them to it,
as it says: "I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:19. This is the same פסוק of the trees from Step 8.

phrases.english: and "wilderness" means nothing other than Jerusalem,
as it says: "Zion has become a wilderness, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל שִׁיטָּה וְשִׁיטָּה שֶׁנָּטְלוּ גּוֹיִם מִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the coral side-discussion and returns to the פסוק of the trees in ישעיהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב"ה will return to ירושלים every acacia tree that the nations took from it.

steps.title: One who learns but does not teach is like a myrtle in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that someone who learns תורה but does not teach it is like a הדס in the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Anyone who learns תורה and does not teach it is like a myrtle in the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second teaching. It uses the הדס, which is also in the פסוק of the trees, as a picture of a person who learns תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A myrtle has a lovely smell, but out in the wilderness nobody is around to enjoy it. In the same way, a person who keeps his תורה to himself has something good that does not reach anyone else.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anyone who learns Torah and does not teach it
is like a myrtle in the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ מְלַמְּדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן, again drawn from a tree in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who learns תורה but does not teach it is like a myrtle in the wilderness, whose good smell goes to waste.

steps.title: Another version: teaching where there are no scholars is precious
steps.stepSummary: Others report רבי יוחנן's teaching the opposite way. Someone who learns and teaches where there are no תלמידי חכמים is like a precious myrtle in the wilderness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: Anyone who learns תורה and teaches it in a place where there are no תלמידי חכמים is like a myrtle in the wilderness, which is precious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי יוחנן's statement. Here the same picture, a myrtle in the wilderness, is used as praise instead of criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the myrtle in the wilderness is wasted because nobody smells it. In this version it is especially treasured because it is rare there. So a person who teaches תורה where there are no other scholars is very precious.

keyTerms.meaning: some say, there is another version

steps.confusionAlert: The same picture, "a myrtle in the wilderness," means opposite things in the two versions. In the first it is a criticism, because the smell is wasted. In the second it is praise, because the myrtle is rare and precious.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's myrtle comes in two versions. Either it is a criticism of someone who learns and does not teach, or it is praise for someone who teaches where there are no other scholars.

phrases.english: Some say it this way:
Anyone who learns Torah and teaches it
in a place where there are no Torah scholars
is like a myrtle in the wilderness, which is precious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כׇּל הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה וּמְלַמְּדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 17, turning the myrtle picture into praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learns and teaches תורה where there are no other scholars is precious, like a myrtle in the wilderness.

steps.title: Nothing can replace רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says woe to the nations, because they have no way to fix what they did. Metal can be paid back with better metal, but nothing can replace רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said: Woe to the nations, because they have no way to fix what they did. The פסוק says: 'Instead of copper I will bring gold, instead of iron silver, instead of wood copper, and instead of stones iron.' Anything stolen can be paid back with something better. But what can they bring instead of רבי עקיבא and his colleagues? About them the פסוק says: 'I will clear them, but their blood I will not clear.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives another teaching. Stolen things can be paid back with something better, but the killing of רבי עקיבא and his colleagues can never be paid back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיהו shows that every stolen material has a more valuable replacement, so material damage can always be repaid. רבי עקיבא and his colleagues have no replacement at all. The פסוק in יואל backs this up: other sins may be cleared, but their blood will not be.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy, a way to fix or make up for something
רבי עקיבא and his colleagues, the great חכמים killed by the Romans
And I will clear (them), declare them free of guilt

steps.whatToRemember: Material losses can always be repaid with something better, but the loss of תלמידי חכמים like רבי עקיבא can never be repaid.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Woe to the nations,
for they have no remedy,
as it says:
"Instead of copper I will bring gold,
and instead of iron I will bring silver,
and instead of wood, copper,
and instead of stones, iron."
But instead of Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
what can they bring?!
And about them it says:
"I will clear them, but their blood I will not clear."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי יוחנן, continuing his teachings about the nations and the final redemption from step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nations can repay any material loss with something better, but there is no repayment for killing רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what is בית בלתין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the mountains where the signal torches were lit, ending with בית בלתין, and asks what that place is. רב begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And from where would they light the torches... and from בית בלתין.' What is בית בלתין? רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the torch signals and asks what the place called בית בלתין is. This sets up רב's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The run of side teachings that started with the coral and the שיטה trees is over, and the גמרא returns to explaining the words of the משנה. It does not question the law here. It only asks what the unfamiliar place name בית בלתין refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Lighting signal torches (to announce the new month)
Short for וכולי, meaning 'etc.', the rest of the quote
The last mountain or place named in the משנה's chain of torch stations

phrases.english: "And from where would they light the torches, etc.
and from Beit Biltin."
What is Beit Biltin?
Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side teachings and goes back to explaining the משנה's list of torch stations
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the place called בית בלתין mentioned in the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב begins to answer; his answer continues on the next amud
